page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: Respon. Non est. Ratio: quia promissiones externæ habent conditionem perseverantiæ Ecclesiæ in fide & pœnitentia, quam nos abjicimus.
Propositio. Sunt igitur aliæ causæ spectantes ad nostram salutem & ad gloriam Dei.
I. Peccata nostra, quæ militant adversus nos, specificentur præcipua profanitas: contemtus Dei & religionis, securitas, luxus, superbia, &c. Ergo juste affligimur.
Amplific. exemplo Israelitarum, qui cum essent populus Dei, sæpius sibi attraxerunt graves calamitates suis peccatis.
II. Castigatio ad resipiscentiam: ne cum mundo pereamus 1. Cor.11. Domino corripimur.
III. Exercitium patientiæ, fidei, spei pioru. 1.Pet.1. Ut τὸ δοκίμιον fidei vestræ.
IV. Humilitas nostra: ut humiliati deponamus cristas, & de nostra petentia desperantes à Deo pendere & victoriam petere discamus.
Amplif. a fine: Dei potentiam in liberatione Ecclesiæ esse illustriorem ubi desperatum est de causis secundis: Exemplo Israelitarum ad mare rubrum.
V. Declaratio amoris Dei erga Ecclesiam sub cruce contra potentes hostes eam nihilominus servantis.
VI. Declaratio illustrior justitiæ Dei in punitis hostibus, postquam diu eos toleravit & [illegible, ~8 letters]- γίτες reddidit.

page.notes: The Greek word after "&" at the end of the last paragraph and the Greek word that starts the next line are not clearly legible; the ending of the second line appears to read "γίτες" or "γηρες". The Greek word "ἑξῆς" after "Sequatur" is uncertain. The Greek "τὸ δοκίμιον" is read from a small, slanted print and may differ slightly. "Spe" and "cificentur" are split across a line end without a printed hyphen, so the word is written whole. The Roman numerals are copied as printed, with spaces in "I I I." etc. normalised to "III.", "II.", "IV.", "VI.". The "Ratio:" and "Amplific." marks are printed in italic or a different type and are taken as italic. The "Confir-" catchword carries a printed hyphen.
